stem: What is the most common side effect of stimulant medications in children with ADHD?

options.text: Loss of appetite, particularly at lunchtime
Permanent growth delay and height restriction

explanation: Loss of appetite, particularly at lunchtime, is the most common side effect of stimulant medications, and many children make up for this with better intake later in the day.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because loss of appetite, especially around lunchtime, is the most common stimulant side effect and children often eat more later in the day.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because stimulant treatment has not been shown to cause permanent growth delay in most children, and this was not the most common side effect described.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because tics are more often part of the underlying condition or comorbidity than a common stimulant side effect.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because stimulant medicines require cardiovascular screening, but they do not commonly cause heart disease.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because stimulants more commonly reduce appetite than cause severe daytime sleepiness.

source.hint: Focus on a side effect related to a basic daily biological necessity that often returns to normal in the evening.
